subject.title: fix(agents): repair orphaned tool_use pairs on compaction prune path

question: Should compaction use the same aborted-turn drop policy as prompt-send sanitization for orphaned tool-use turns, or should it preserve the turn by synthesizing an interrupted tool result?
rationale: Both shapes can make provider transcripts valid, but they encode different session-state semantics: dropping avoids fabricated tool output, while synthesizing preserves more context but may mislead the summarizer.

options.title: Accept drop policy
options.body: Merge the current fix and treat aborted assistant tool-call turns as invalid compaction input that should be removed before summarization.

options.title: Require synthetic interrupted result
options.body: Ask the contributor to preserve the assistant turn with an explicit synthetic interrupted result and focused tests for that policy.

options.title: Defer broader recovery design
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers decide a richer session recovery contract for interrupted tool calls.

recommendation.title: Accept drop policy
recommendation.body: Merge the current fix and treat aborted assistant tool-call turns as invalid compaction input that should be removed before summarization.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc recently merged adjacent orphaned-tool-use handling and has recent history in the session transcript repair path.
